links.outcome: Concordance of ChatGPT drug safety classification with Micromedex for kidney disease patients
links.effect: Agreement with Micromedex was 64.5% for ChatGPT-3.5 and 81.4% for ChatGPT-4. ChatGPT-3.5 flagged 11 (8.9%) as potentially harmful versus Micromedex 35 (28.2%).
links.quote: The overall agreement between Micromedex and ChatGPT-3.5 was 64.5% and ChatGPT-4 demonstrated a higher agreement at 81.4%.

links.outcome: Accuracy of LLM safety assessments against reference standard (Micromedex)
links.effect: ChatGPT-3.5 agreement 64.5%, ChatGPT-4 81.4%; ChatGPT-3.5 lower concordance for supplements at 60.3%. Neither model recommended as a reliable drug information source.
links.quote: Neither ChatGPT-3.5 nor ChatGPT-4 can be currently recommended as reliable drug information sources for this demographic.

screen.reason: Empirical benchmark evaluating ChatGPT-3.5 and ChatGPT-4 accuracy/concordance against Micromedex for kidney disease medication and supplement safety queries, with no deployment practice tested.
